items.title: Bill Huntington and Charlie Suhor Interview, 1992-04-06
items.q: I went and played a lot with Al Baleto and played at the Playboy Clubs with these various great piano players like Rusty and like John Probst

ctx.x: Somebody I should mention just because he is sort of a grandparent-like link with so many of the players of the time is a drummer named Lou Dillon, who's now the retiring business agent. He was a damn good teacher. He played some jazz well, played Latin music, played show drums, a good show drummer. But he taught Reed Vaughn when Reed was just kind of bumping around trying to find a style. I know Lou. He's nice. Okay. Reed then said you've got to take lessons from this guy I'm taking from, because Reed was…
Rusty Main, who was an incredible player.

Yeah. But the list, I just wanted to get a sense of my view of who some of the leaders were, who people look to for innovation, you know, perhaps, again, your list might be different, Bill, but I wanted to get that on the table. Sure. Yours.
